To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TAST and Arcans tests can be used for the evaluation of the nonlinear behavior (shear stress–shear strain curves) of adhesives.

the Arcan fixture is a more reliable test method for adhesives than the TAST fixture, and that a modified TAST fixture, in which the adherends are cut at an angle of 45 degrees, can provide a more homogeneous stress field in the adhesive joint.
the nonlinear behavior of structural adhesives is not correctly analyzed by the standard TAST test and that this can be corrected by using a modified TAST test or an Arcan test.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison between two types of shear tests for adhesively bonded joints.
the development of new experimental techniques and numerical models for the characterization of the behavior of structural adhesives and adhesive joints.
the development of new test fixtures for adhesively bonded joints, which are able to take into account the nonlinearity of the adhesive and its finite deformations, as well as to avoid edge effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Arcan is better than TAST for the analysis of the adhesive behavior in bonded assemblies, particularly when an adhesive mode failure is expected.
, when the TAST test is used, a careful analysis of the failure mode is required to avoid erroneous results.
the TAST specimen is not recommended for the characterization of structural adhesives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TAST test is not a reliable method for the characterization of the shear behavior of adhesively bonded joints, particularly when the adhesive is brittle.
a TAST fixture can provide useful data for a given adhesive–substrate system if the test is conducted in the linear elastic regime.
the Arcan fixture provides more reliable results for the analysis of the shear strength of adhesives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when testing adhesives with a TAST fixture, the failure initiation zone must be taken into account in the interpretation of the results.
the Arcan test is a good alternative to the TAST test for studying the shear behavior of adhesively bonded joints.
the TAST test should be used only with great care and with a full knowledge of the failure modes of the adhesive.
